historical_record.description: The Office of the Assessor-Recorder photographed the property for tax assessment. Grabhorn Press was at the address.

A two-storey brick building 27 by 120 feet was put up as an annex and classroom wing to the temple school next door, designed by Alfred Henry Jacobs, who had designed the 1910 school at 1337 Sutter Street as well. Its stuccoed front is divided into three equal bays by tall Doric columns, with plate-glass display windows in two and a pair of glazed oak doors in the third, bas-relief panels above the clerestories, and a standing-seam copper mansard behind.
The congregation had owned the two buildings on one lot since 1911; when its school moved out to the new temple at Lake and Arguello, both passed to a real estate firm.

The lot was split in two and the smaller building bought by the Grabhorn family, who moved the Grabhorn Press into it in the autumn. Edwin and Robert Grabhorn had printed in San Francisco since 1919, at Kearny Street, Powell Street, Pine Street and Commercial Street in turn; Sutter Street held them longer than anywhere else. The press room took most of the ground floor with a corner for typesetting, the bindery and office were upstairs, and paper was kept in the basement.

The press was disbanded at the end of the year. Nearly half of everything it ever printed — numbers 379 to 654 of the 654 items its bibliographies record — was set and printed in this building, among them the Japanese prints and the nine Shakespeare plays, in editions of 185 copies with coloured woodcuts by Mary Grabhorn.

The interior was reworked for a gym over 1982 and 1983: partitions and bathrooms moved, mirrors run along the east wall of both floors, a chrome slatted ceiling dropped six inches below the original on the first floor, and three steps just inside the entrance rebuilt.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places at statewide level for its place in twentieth-century Californian fine printing.

hook: A 1918 temple-school annex that the Grabhorn Press printed in from 1942 to 1965.
